evals.name: split-from-plan
evals.prompt: We just finished planning milestone 3 of ledger; the plan is in plan.md. lets see how we split the work between different workers, and according to the projected complexity decide if it should be a sonnet or opus agent
evals.expected_output: A wave-ordered worker table with disjoint file ownership, dependencies, complexity reason and model per task, a mechanics section with the invariant rules for every prompt, and a closing go question. No launch.
assertions: Reply contains a worker table with per-task owned files, complexity, and model, and each task's dependencies are stated either in a column or in the wave heading it sits under
Tasks are grouped into numbered waves derived from dependencies; the first worker wave depends on no other worker task (a coordinator wave 0 is allowed)
File ownership across tasks is disjoint: no path appears under two different tasks
Every task row, including low-complexity ones, gives a reason for its model choice, not only a rating word
Opus is assigned to the tasks that can silently lose or corrupt data (same-transaction audit stamp, exporter watermark/commit order)
Reply lists the milestone invariants that go into every worker prompt (audit_daily is the only per-day aggregation; src/audit never imports src/ui)
Reply states what the coordinator keeps for itself (merge order, checks it runs, wiring) and whether deploys happen between waves
Reply ends with a go question inviting changes to the split, and no worker prompt files or launch commands exist in the outputs directory
Reply lists the plan's open gaps (for example the audit_daily view body) with a proposed answer for each, instead of deciding them silently
Every module listed in the plan's Modules section is assigned to exactly one task or to the coordinator

evals.name: go-writes-prompts
evals.prompt: Plan is in plan.md, the split we agreed on is in agreed-split.md. cool, spin up workers (opus / sonnet depending on the complexity) to implement this. Note for this test environment: the superset CLI is not available here, so write the worker prompt files you would launch with into the outputs directory, plus a launch.md with the exact commands you would run and the coordinator table, then stop.
evals.expected_output: A common.md with role, read-first list, repo conventions, milestone rules, live-resource safety, and the DONE/BLOCKED envelopes; one prompt file per task with Deliver and Verify sections and exact paths; launch.md with per-task model and wave-1-only launches; wave-2 prompts prepared but not launched.
assertions: A shared common.md exists with worker role and worktree/branch rules, read-first list, repo conventions, the milestone rules, live-database safety, and both SUPERSET_WORKER_DONE and SUPERSET_WORKER_BLOCKED envelopes
One prompt file exists per task in the agreed split (A1..A6)
Each task prompt has a Deliver section with exact file paths and a Verify section with at least one task-specific command beyond the generic test run
Task prompts for A3 name the local stand-in or the merged dependency shapes it needs from A1/A2
launch.md launches only the wave-1 tasks (A1, A2) now and holds A3..A6 until their dependencies merge
launch.md assigns the model per task exactly as in agreed-split.md (A1 Opus, A2 Sonnet, A3 Opus, A4 Sonnet, A5 Sonnet, A6 Sonnet)
launch.md contains a coordinator table with Task, Model, Branch/Workspace, and State columns
Commit message instruction in common.md includes the Co-Authored-By attribution line from the plan
Task IDs, owned paths, and models in the prompts match agreed-split.md, and any added path is called out in the reply or launch.md
No final plan decision is overridden in the prompts without the reply flagging it to the user

evals.name: orchestrate-request-without-split
evals.prompt: the plan for ledger milestone 3 is in plan.md. use superset:orchestrate to spin up agents (opus) to implement this. Note for this test environment: the superset CLI is not available here; if you reach the point of launching, write what you would launch into the outputs directory instead.
evals.expected_output: The skill presents the split table first and stops for the user's go instead of launching; all tasks on Opus as requested but the complexity column is kept.
assertions: Reply presents a split table (tasks, owned files, dependencies, waves) and ends the turn without launching
Reply stops and asks the user for a go instead of launching or writing launch commands
All tasks are assigned Opus as the user requested, and the reply names which tasks would be Sonnet under the default rule
A complexity or risk column is still present so the user can see where risk sits
No worker prompt files or launch commands were written to the outputs directory
File ownership across tasks is disjoint: no path appears under two different tasks
Reply lists the plan's open gaps with a proposed answer for each instead of deciding them silently
